questions.prompt: All human beings belong to the species called ______.
questions.explanation: The answer is Homo sapiens.

questions.prompt: Small differences between members of the same species are called ______.
questions.explanation: The answer is variations.

questions.prompt: Height and weight are examples of ______ variation.
questions.explanation: The answer is continuous.

questions.prompt: Tongue rolling and eye colour are examples of ______ variation.
questions.explanation: The answer is discontinuous.

questions.prompt: A tan gained from sunlight is an example of ______ variation.
questions.explanation: The answer is acquired.

questions.prompt: A bell-shaped graph of a feature in a population is called a normal ______ curve.
questions.explanation: The answer is distribution.

questions.prompt: A thick fat layer under a polar bear's skin is called ______.
questions.explanation: The answer is blubber.

questions.prompt: Blending into the surroundings to hide is called ______.
questions.explanation: The answer is camouflage.

questions.prompt: A cactus's leaves are reduced to ______ to cut water loss.
questions.explanation: The answer is spines.

questions.prompt: A camel's hump stores ______ as an energy reserve.
questions.explanation: The answer is fat.

questions.prompt: The process that turns beneficial variations into adaptations is called natural ______.
questions.explanation: The answer is selection.

questions.prompt: The passing of characteristics from parents to offspring is called ______.
questions.explanation: The answer is heredity.

questions.prompt: The scientist who founded genetics using garden peas was Gregor ______.
questions.explanation: The answer is Mendel.

questions.prompt: The basic units of heredity are called ______.
questions.explanation: The answer is genes.

questions.prompt: Thread-like structures in the nucleus that carry genes are called ______.
questions.explanation: The answer is chromosomes.

questions.prompt: Different forms of the same gene are called ______.
questions.explanation: The answer is alleles.

questions.prompt: An organism with two identical alleles (BB or bb) is called ______.
questions.explanation: The answer is homozygous.

questions.prompt: An organism with two different alleles (Bb) is called ______.
questions.explanation: The answer is heterozygous.

questions.prompt: DNA stands for ______ acid.
questions.explanation: The answer is deoxyribonucleic.

questions.prompt: The twisted-ladder shape of DNA is called a double ______.
questions.explanation: The answer is helix.

questions.prompt: In DNA, Adenine always pairs with ______.
questions.explanation: The answer is Thymine.

questions.prompt: In DNA, Cytosine always pairs with ______.
questions.explanation: The answer is Guanine.

questions.prompt: The building block of DNA is called a ______.
questions.explanation: The answer is nucleotide.

questions.prompt: Cell division for growth and repair is called ______.
questions.explanation: The answer is mitosis.

questions.prompt: The longest stage of the cell cycle is ______.
questions.explanation: The answer is interphase.

questions.prompt: When DNA makes an exact copy of itself it is called ______.
questions.explanation: The answer is replication.

questions.prompt: The four stages of mitosis are prophase, metaphase, anaphase and ______.
questions.explanation: The answer is telophase.

questions.prompt: Cell division that makes four gametes with half the chromosome number is called ______.
questions.explanation: The answer is meiosis.

questions.prompt: Sex cells produced by meiosis are called ______.
questions.explanation: The answer is gametes.

questions.prompt: A body cell with the full chromosome number is described as ______.
questions.explanation: The answer is diploid.

questions.prompt: A gamete with half the chromosome number is described as ______.
questions.explanation: The answer is haploid.

questions.prompt: The cell formed when sperm and egg fuse is called a ______.
questions.explanation: The answer is zygote.

questions.prompt: A change in the DNA of a cell is called a ______.
questions.explanation: The answer is mutation.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: the scientific name for all human beings, the only surviving human species.
questions.explanation: Homo sapiens: the scientific name for all human beings, the only surviving human species.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: a group of living things with similar features that can reproduce together.
questions.explanation: Species: a group of living things with similar features that can reproduce together.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: the small differences between individual members of the same species.
questions.explanation: Variation: the small differences between individual members of the same species.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: variation where a feature can take any value in a range, e.g. height and weight.
questions.explanation: Continuous variation: variation where a feature can take any value in a range, e.g. height and weight.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: variation where features fall into distinct separate groups, e.g. tongue rolling and eye colour.
questions.explanation: Discontinuous variation: variation where features fall into distinct separate groups, e.g. tongue rolling and eye colour.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: variation gained during a lifetime from the environment or activities, not passed from parents.
questions.explanation: Acquired variation: variation gained during a lifetime from the environment or activities, not passed from parents.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: a bell-shaped graph in which most values cluster near the average.
questions.explanation: Normal distribution curve: a bell-shaped graph in which most values cluster near the average.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: a feature controlled by a dominant allele that appears more often in a population.
questions.explanation: Dominant characteristic: a feature controlled by a dominant allele that appears more often in a population.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: a physical or behavioural feature that helps an organism survive in its environment.
questions.explanation: Adaptation: a physical or behavioural feature that helps an organism survive in its environment.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: extremely cold conditions near the North Pole.
questions.explanation: Arctic conditions: extremely cold conditions near the North Pole.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: a thick fat layer under the skin that provides insulation and an energy store.
questions.explanation: Blubber: a thick fat layer under the skin that provides insulation and an energy store.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: blending into the surroundings to hide from predators or prey.
questions.explanation: Camouflage: blending into the surroundings to hide from predators or prey.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: a material that reduces heat transfer, such as blubber and fur.
questions.explanation: Insulation: a material that reduces heat transfer, such as blubber and fur.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: a waxy protective coating on a plant surface that reduces water loss.
questions.explanation: Cuticle: a waxy protective coating on a plant surface that reduces water loss.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: to enter deep sleep in winter to conserve energy, with body temperature and metabolism dropping.
questions.explanation: Hibernate: to enter deep sleep in winter to conserve energy, with body temperature and metabolism dropping.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: a sweet liquid in flowers that attracts insects for pollination.
questions.explanation: Nectar: a sweet liquid in flowers that attracts insects for pollination.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: the transfer of pollen between flowers, needed for plant reproduction.
questions.explanation: Pollination: the transfer of pollen between flowers, needed for plant reproduction.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: the process by which organisms with beneficial variations survive and reproduce more successfully.
questions.explanation: Natural selection: the process by which organisms with beneficial variations survive and reproduce more successfully.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: the young produced by an organism, the next generation.
questions.explanation: Offspring: the young produced by an organism, the next generation.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: the passing of characteristics from parents to offspring through genes.
questions.explanation: Heredity: the passing of characteristics from parents to offspring through genes.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: the scientific study of how heredity works.
questions.explanation: Genetics: the scientific study of how heredity works.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: a unit of hereditary information on a chromosome that controls one or more characteristics.
questions.explanation: Gene: a unit of hereditary information on a chromosome that controls one or more characteristics.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: a thread-like structure in the cell nucleus, made of DNA, that carries many genes.
questions.explanation: Chromosome: a thread-like structure in the cell nucleus, made of DNA, that carries many genes.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: the Austrian scientist (1822-1884) who founded genetics through garden pea experiments.
questions.explanation: Gregor Mendel: the Austrian scientist (1822-1884) who founded genetics through garden pea experiments.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: a different form of the same gene, e.g. a black-hair allele and a blond-hair allele.
questions.explanation: Allele: a different form of the same gene, e.g. a black-hair allele and a blond-hair allele.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: the more powerful allele that shows its effect even when only one copy is present.
questions.explanation: Dominant allele: the more powerful allele that shows its effect even when only one copy is present.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: the weaker allele that is only expressed when two copies are present with no dominant allele.
questions.explanation: Recessive allele: the weaker allele that is only expressed when two copies are present with no dominant allele.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: having two identical alleles for the same characteristic, e.g. BB or bb (also called pure bred).
questions.explanation: Homozygous: having two identical alleles for the same characteristic, e.g. BB or bb (also called pure bred).

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: having two different alleles, one dominant and one recessive, e.g. Bb (also called hybrid).
questions.explanation: Heterozygous: having two different alleles, one dominant and one recessive, e.g. Bb (also called hybrid).

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: the actual genetic makeup of an organism, the combination of alleles it carries.
questions.explanation: Genotype: the actual genetic makeup of an organism, the combination of alleles it carries.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: the physical, observable characteristic, e.g. black hair.
questions.explanation: Phenotype: the physical, observable characteristic, e.g. black hair.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: deoxyribonucleic acid, the chemical that makes up genes and chromosomes.
questions.explanation: DNA: deoxyribonucleic acid, the chemical that makes up genes and chromosomes.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: the twisted-ladder shape of a DNA molecule.
questions.explanation: Double helix: the twisted-ladder shape of a DNA molecule.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: the building block of DNA, made of a deoxyribose sugar, a phosphate group and an organic base.
questions.explanation: Nucleotide: the building block of DNA, made of a deoxyribose sugar, a phosphate group and an organic base.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: the five-carbon sugar forming the backbone of DNA.
questions.explanation: Deoxyribose: the five-carbon sugar forming the backbone of DNA.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: a chemical group forming one side of the DNA backbone.
questions.explanation: Phosphate group: a chemical group forming one side of the DNA backbone.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: the sequence of A, T, C and G bases in DNA that codes for all characteristics of an organism.
questions.explanation: Genetic code: the sequence of A, T, C and G bases in DNA that codes for all characteristics of an organism.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: cell division that produces two identical daughter cells, used for growth and repair.
questions.explanation: Mitosis: cell division that produces two identical daughter cells, used for growth and repair.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: DNA making an exact copy of itself before cell division.
questions.explanation: Replication: DNA making an exact copy of itself before cell division.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: the stage when a cell is not dividing and prepares by replicating its DNA.
questions.explanation: Interphase: the stage when a cell is not dividing and prepares by replicating its DNA.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: the mitosis stage where chromosomes become visible and the nuclear membrane breaks down.
questions.explanation: Prophase: the mitosis stage where chromosomes become visible and the nuclear membrane breaks down.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: the mitosis stage where the spindle forms and chromosomes line up in the middle.
questions.explanation: Metaphase: the mitosis stage where the spindle forms and chromosomes line up in the middle.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: the mitosis stage where spindle fibres pull the chromatids to opposite ends.
questions.explanation: Anaphase: the mitosis stage where spindle fibres pull the chromatids to opposite ends.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: the mitosis stage where nuclear membranes reform, the cytoplasm divides and two daughter cells form.
questions.explanation: Telophase: the mitosis stage where nuclear membranes reform, the cytoplasm divides and two daughter cells form.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: the two identical copies of a chromosome joined together after DNA replication.
questions.explanation: Chromatids: the two identical copies of a chromosome joined together after DNA replication.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: the protein-fibre structure that pulls chromosomes apart during cell division.
questions.explanation: Spindle: the protein-fibre structure that pulls chromosomes apart during cell division.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: the new cells produced by division; in mitosis they are genetically identical to the parent.
questions.explanation: Daughter cells: the new cells produced by division; in mitosis they are genetically identical to the parent.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: the jelly-like substance inside the cell membrane surrounding the nucleus.
questions.explanation: Cytoplasm: the jelly-like substance inside the cell membrane surrounding the nucleus.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: cell division that produces four sex cells (gametes) with half the chromosome number.
questions.explanation: Meiosis: cell division that produces four sex cells (gametes) with half the chromosome number.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: sex cells (egg and sperm) produced by meiosis, containing half the chromosome number.
questions.explanation: Gametes: sex cells (egg and sperm) produced by meiosis, containing half the chromosome number.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: the fusion of a sperm and an egg to form a new cell (zygote).
questions.explanation: Fertilisation: the fusion of a sperm and an egg to form a new cell (zygote).

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: the cell formed when sperm and egg fuse, having the full chromosome number (2n).
questions.explanation: Zygote: the cell formed when sperm and egg fuse, having the full chromosome number (2n).

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: having the full chromosome number (2n), two sets, one from each parent.
questions.explanation: Diploid: having the full chromosome number (2n), two sets, one from each parent.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: having half the chromosome number (n), as in gametes produced by meiosis.
questions.explanation: Haploid: having half the chromosome number (n), as in gametes produced by meiosis.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: an organism genetically identical to its parent, produced by asexual reproduction (mitosis).
questions.explanation: Clone: an organism genetically identical to its parent, produced by asexual reproduction (mitosis).

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: the division of cytoplasm at the end of cell division to produce two separate cells.
questions.explanation: Cytokinesis: the division of cytoplasm at the end of cell division to produce two separate cells.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: a change in the genetic information (DNA sequence) of a cell.
questions.explanation: Mutation: a change in the genetic information (DNA sequence) of a cell.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: a mutation affecting one gene, changing the instructions for one characteristic.
questions.explanation: Single gene mutation: a mutation affecting one gene, changing the instructions for one characteristic.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: a mutation affecting the structure of one or more chromosomes, which is more severe.
questions.explanation: Chromosome mutation: a mutation affecting the structure of one or more chromosomes, which is more severe.

questions.prompt: ______ is defined as: a mutation that gives a survival advantage and can become an adaptation through natural selection.
questions.explanation: Beneficial mutation: a mutation that gives a survival advantage and can become an adaptation through natural selection.
